column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1 on SDK 20.5.17, update 1.0.1; 73,512 shaders, all translated. Its shader libraries are in the IoStore container, Oodle-compressed shader groups that the port
# decodes with the game's own Oodle on the device (porter device_ue: one round, 5,919 groups, 74,244 shaders in 44 s), so the port needs the device connected.
# Tested 2026-11-06 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), docked (1920x1080): the brightness setting, the title, a new game (difficulty), the
# opening cinematic, the first road (walking, tutorials), the cutscene, the first battle's command menu; an autosave, and Continue from it after a restart.
# 60 fps (the profile's fps_target): frame work p50 about 16.5 ms, GPU 10-13 ms in the field and the cinematic, 0-6 dropped frames per 300; 0 audio underruns; one red line
# in some runs: an R32F buffer texture of 44 elements at an offset 8 bytes past a multiple of 64 (Adreno's minTexelBufferOffsetAlignment, no single-texel relaxation), read as zeros.
# Open: the fires in the first battle's background (the battle tutorial's picture shows them) are not drawn; no draw is skipped (no program, target or pipeline missing), and
# every indirect draw's arguments are in the pools. Ruled out: culling (DM_VK_NOCULL=1), the particle vertex factories' dynamic texture slots (android_dynamic_slots on), the
# misaligned buffer texture (a view 8 bytes early, test build: no change). Next: the Niagara simulation's submission (about 60 dispatches over one data buffer, cleared and
# copied each frame) and whether the CPU sees its counts (copied pools merge back only tracked GPU writes).
